label: Today You Will Learn
h: How to tell forced optimism and unsupported reassurance from biblical renewal, and replace one reassurance with a sentence that is true.
body:
About 8 minutes, plus one short pause · one small practice · no homework list

Persistent low mood or hopelessness deserves a doctor's assessment, not another attempt at thinking well. Hopelessness that includes thoughts of suicide or self-harm needs urgent help today.

label: Key Scripture
h: "Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may discern what is the will of God."

label: Meet Naomi
h: "I am saying all the right things, and I feel like a liar. And I cannot plan anything, because planning would be doubting."
body: <svg class="art" viewBox="0 0 360 180" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="90" y="30" width="180" height="120" rx="10" fill="#3b4a60"/><rect x="100" y="40" width="160" height="100" rx="6" fill="#2a3749"/><text x="180" y="95" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" fill="#b9c0cb">ACCOUNTS</text><g class="lockg"><rect x="160" y="112" width="40" height="30" rx="5" fill="#c78a2c"/><path d="M168 112v-10a12 12 0 0 1 24 0v10" fill="none" stroke="#c78a2c" stroke-width="5"/></g><text x="180" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#b9c0cb">"planning would be doubting"</text></svg>

label: Four Things Mistaken For Renewal
body:
DenialRefuses to look at what is true because it is painful.
False reassuranceSays something comforting that may not be true, then repeats it louder.
Forced optimismTreats any negative expectation as a failure of faith. Cannot plan.
SuppressionPushes the thought down and lays a hopeful sentence over it.

Each makes peace depend on the situation turning out well.

label: A Common Belief
h: "If I acknowledge the problem, I am agreeing with it."
body: To say "the company may close" is to describe a possibility accurately, so it can be prayed about and prepared for.

label: The Main Truth · What Renewal Sounds Like
body:
"It will be fine."→"I do not know how this will turn out. God knows, and he is with me in it."
"I must not think about failure."→"The company may close. If it does, we will grieve, we will need a plan, and God will still be God."

A true sentence does not have to be defended.

label: A Caution About Promises
h: Not every promise in Scripture was made to every reader in every circumstance.
body: What is promised: God's presence, forgiveness, sustaining grace, resurrection, life with Christ. Not every outcome you want.

label: The Practice
body:
1. Write down the sentences you have been using to comfort yourself. Exactly.
  2. Test each: true? the whole truth? has God said this?
  3. Rewrite the ones that fail as sentences that are true.
  4. Do what the true sentence permits.

label: Do This Now
h: Write one reassurance you have been repeating. Under it, write the sentence that is actually true.
body:
Then name one step the true sentence permits. If the matter is dangerous, medical, legal or financial, that step is asking the right person for help.

Pause the audio

label: Remember
h: A renewed mind weeps truthfully and hopes truthfully at the same time.

label: Prayer
body:
Father, I do not know
how this will turn out.

You know, and you are with me in it.

Renew my mind, so that I can see clearly
and still hope.

Amen.
